02 · FOLLOW THE RECORDS

One decision at a time
Restart both traces

One comparison is the recipe’s “is this key smaller?” decision. One exchange swaps two distinct positions. These are operation counts, not measured running times.

Draft changed. Start a new comparison to use these records.

Equal keys make the difference visible.

Try the first example. Selection’s distant exchange can move one tied record past another, even though the final keys are sorted.

03 · RECALL, EXPLAIN, TRANSFER

Take the twelve-question lesson

Practice record identity, insertion’s equal-key rule, selection’s distant exchange and the meaning of operation counts.

Download the course, open the RecallWeave learner, choose the course file and inspect its preview. Starting the imported course explicitly begins the new lesson. You can then review your first answers, practice misses and download study notes.
